## Epic red-line read · 2026-11-12T22:15Z

Head-sha: `b2ca1d5414fd81429dd417c8959302c171151801` (main 2fc3fce5 merged). Read-only.
Verdict: **PASS-with-nits.** Nothing must be fixed. The reason for striking item 4 holds; one sentence of it is too wide (nit 1).

- **Red line 1, resolution not loosened:** holds. Only `@object-ui/app-shell` changes; no server file is touched. Each change takes away a control (a Remove, the position hint) that the row could not use. No request is sent that was not sent before.
- **Red line 2, ambiguity reported, never guessed:** holds.
  - A one-candidate refusal on Add shows one button, and nothing more is sent until it is clicked (item 1).
  - An empty candidate list gives no pick, only the server's sentence (item 2).
  - The environment's button re-sends by name alone, only for the users still to grant (item 4).
  - A grant row with no id never takes the place of the same user's removable grant, in either save order.
- **Red line 3, independently releasable:** holds.
  - The repo's reader (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`) reads `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` from both the body and the changeset.
  - The changeset is a `patch`, and the change is not breaking, so no ADR-0087 entry is owed.
  - The Items table and the changeset state each FROM→TO, and they match the diff.
- **The merge:** `git show --remerge-diff` of b2ca1d54 is empty. It merged #32804 and #32819, and neither touches these files.

### Item 4: is striking it right?

It is. **A grant that names no package is never refused naming the environment.** Measured:

- **Bare grants, on the card thread's real-engine rig** (real ObjectQL, an SQL driver, the grant-name hook and the stamp seam; a stand-in registry):

  | State | Answer |
  |:--|:--|
  | Two packages hold the name, no environment item | 409 `ambiguous-in-environment`, naming the two packages only |
  | One package | Stored with that package |
  | The environment only | Stored, package null |
  | Two packages plus the environment | Stored, package null |

- **A grant naming a package that does not hold the set**, on the same rig: 409 `not-held-by-qualifier`, naming the environment (and the packages). The bare re-send is stored with package null. This reproduces the card thread's log.
- **The metadata store's bare read of a `permission` set**, across five save orders: never names the environment. With two packages plus a package-less row it is 409 naming the two packages in all three orders.
  - An `action`'s bare read does name the environment when the package-less row is saved last.
  - So the claim holds because `permission` is not an owner-keyed type. Only `action` is.
- **Read in the code, not measured:**
  - `resolveEnvironmentWide` never lists the environment as a candidate.
  - The stamp seam's bare path stamps the row and never refuses it.
  - The `outside-closure` refusal that names the environment needs a caller package, and a bare grant from this page has none.

Measured at head:
- `AssignedUsersSection.holderPick-32807.test.tsx`: 6/6.
- The named metadata-admin suites (the same globs as the body): 57 files, 385 tests, all passed.
- CI at read time: 31 success, 13 skipped, 6 still running (the UI test shards and the UI type check).

Ablations (my own wording of each; baseline 6 green; every file restored to its HEAD blob; the CONTROL stayed green in every red run):

| Ablation | Red / green |
|:--|:--|
| `grantIdOf` returns `String(grant.id)` | 2 / 4 |
| Holder rows' id map: the last grant wins | 1 / 5 |
| Unresolved row's Remove shown without an id | 1 / 5 |
| A direct row with no id shows the position hint | 1 / 5 |
| A one-candidate refusal on Add picks and re-sends by itself | 1 / 5 |
| An empty candidate list is taken as a pick | 1 / 5 |
| The environment's button falls back to the holding's package | 1 / 5 |

Nits (a follow-up card under #32807; no extra round):

1. **One sentence of the item 4 reasoning is too wide:** "So the bare re-send is accepted".
   - It holds where the refusal's candidates come from the registry's list of holders.
   - It does not hold where the registry holds no holder of the name and the security catalog falls back to the metadata service. There, the candidates of a `not-held-by-qualifier` refusal come from `list`, which keeps one entry per name (the finding below). The environment can then be the only button offered.
   - Read, not measured end to end: in that state the bare re-send is refused again, naming the two packages. The pick then changes, so the dead end of #32800's nit 4 does not come back.
2. **A direct grant with no id, for a user also held through a position, shows neither a Remove nor the "held via a position" hint.** The hint would still be true for that row.

Pre-existing on `main`, not changed by this PR; for the seat to route (a card under #32778 or #32774):
- **On the metadata-only path, the catalog's per-holder list of a permission set keeps only the first declared item of each name** (`createSecurityCatalogReader` `list`, `declaredByName`). The metadata-only path is when the registry serves no holder of the name.
- So `judgeGrantSet` accepts a grant that names the first-listed holder, and refuses a grant that names the other real holder, naming only the first.
- Measured with a stand-in metadata list and an empty registry:
  - listed order crm, hr: a grant naming hr is refused, naming crm only;
  - order hr, crm: a grant naming crm is refused, naming hr only;
  - the environment's row listed first: grants naming either package are refused, naming only the environment.
- It fails closed and confers nothing, but list order decides which holder is accepted and which holders are named.
- Not measured: whether a real metadata service lists both packages' slots on that path.
